parts.title: Holiday rental
parts.transcript: Section 1: a woman phones Dave Marriott about renting a vacation cottage. Aster cottage is booked the week of Sept 21 but available the previous week from the 14th, costing $835. Periwinkle Cottage (same price as friends paid last year): part of a historic building first used as a school, then a post office; living room leads onto the deck; river visible from the bedroom; bring own towels; no garage. Town: owner recommends the Chinese restaurant; famous for antique shops. Payment: $200 deposit, final payment by the last day of July.

parts.transcript: Section 2: a co-ordinator briefs volunteers for the Bridge to Brisbane Fun Run. Parking: best at the Jack Gray Sportsfield (not by the river - out of bounds; not the Metro Shopping Complex - they tow). The race number goes on the front of the shirt/singlet; the timing chip clips onto a shoe; everyone wears a wristband. Start order: yellow (elite) first, red (walkers/strollers) last. Still need volunteers to hand out water along the course (first aid covered by St John's Ambulance). Map of Race Village: runners enter bottom-right by corporate catering; Stage (F) on the right along the course; finish line centre; T-shirt Stand (A) at the end of the two paths; Bag Collection (B) top-left on Bowen Road near the exit; Information Centre (H) centre just below the finish line; Prize Draw Box (G) between the shade tents and corporate catering; Water Station (I) left of corporate catering by the third exit to Gregory Terrace.

parts.transcript: Section 3: Joel discusses his research on farmers' attitudes to new agricultural developments with his tutor Dr Owen. He'll specify the location of the farms in the title (A); chose face-to-face interviews to get fuller answers since farmers dislike the phone (C); will ask open questions rather than show a checklist (B). Government communication: much of it is irrelevant - the same info goes to all farmers (A). British farmers have too little time to calculate the costs of new methods (B). Australian sheep farmers make changes based on limited research (B). Book opinions: Contemporary Farming Manual - boring/dull, hard going, no pictures (G); Running a Small Farm - inaccurate, misleading or wrong (E); Agriculture and Economics - essential reading, a required textbook (D); How to Survive in Farming - out of date, written years ago (B).

parts.title: Aboriginal Textile Design
parts.transcript: Section 4: lecture on Aboriginal textile design. Ernabella Arts Centre artists initially made rugs from wool, later batik and screen-printed fabrics. Tiwi Designs early designs included bird images; designs linked to beliefs, e.g. some believed to bring rain. Jimmy Pike: inspired by the Australian landscape, especially the desert; began creating art in prison; his textiles were used to make clothing. Bronwyn Bancroft: a modern look at family and nature; in 1995 painted an athlete's (Cathy Freeman's) jeans with lizards and a rainbow; in 2001 designed a 'Journey of a Nation' parade outfit featuring a snake (no head or tail). Copyright: the 'carpet case' protected Aboriginal artists.
